subject: general
question: The Home Rule League Movement of Bal Gangadhar Tilak had its base across Karnataka and Maharashtra, but excluding which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Home Rule League Movement was started by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** in April 1916 and had its base in Maharashtra and Karnataka.
 
• Tilak’s league aimed at promoting self-governance and instilling nationalist sentiment among Indians through public meetings, campaigns, and outreach efforts.
 
• The movement, though spread across Maharashtra and Karnataka, specifically excluded **Bombay** from its base of operations.
 
• The exclusion of Bombay was due to Tilak’s strategic focus on regions where nationalist sentiment was robust and the likelihood of mass mobilization higher.
 
• Tilak’s Home Rule League primarily focused on rural and semi-urban areas to spread political awareness among the masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Home Rule League Movement:**

 
 
• It was inspired by the Irish Home Rule Movement and aimed at gaining self-rule within the British Empire.
 
• Two Home Rule Leagues operated simultaneously—one led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and the other by Annie Besant.
 
• Annie Besant’s league covered regions like Madras, Bombay, and parts of northern India.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:**
 
 
• Known as the "Father of Indian Unrest," Tilak was a prominent freedom fighter and social reformer.
 
• He popularized the slogan "**Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it**."
 
• Tilak’s efforts were instrumental in mobilizing the masses for India’s independence struggle.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Home Rule Movement:**
 
 
• It significantly contributed to the rise of nationalist sentiment and political consciousness among Indians.
 
• It laid the foundation for future mass movements like the Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience movements.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Movement:**
 
 
• The Home Rule Movement began to decline by 1919 following the introduction of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms and the Rowlatt Act agitation.
 
• Many leaders shifted focus to broader struggles for complete independence.
